top_story: After three consecutive nights of US strikes on Iran beginning by 13 July, Washington shifted from a proposed Hormuz transit toll to an overt blockade, then expanded pressure with strikes on Iranian port-city targets as Tehran retaliated against Bahrain and Jordan. By 15 July, Iran answered by shutting the Strait of Hormuz and threatening to halt all Middle East energy exports, turning a military confrontation into a wider coercive struggle over the region’s commercial lifelines. Tehran’s 16 July warning that the strait is a red line signals that de-escalation space is narrowing as both sides harden positions around maritime control rather than discrete battlefield gains. The immediate effect is to push Gulf states, shipping networks, and households dependent on fuel and trade into the front line of a crisis that now threatens regional economic paralysis as much as direct war.
